title: The Shore That Learned Its Own Stroke

features.name: coast-in-motion
features.desc-on-touch: The shoreline moves as if breathing. Where it touches water, it learns its own rhythm. Sand remembers the stroke.

features.name: swimming-scar
features.desc-on-touch: Where the coast learned to move through water, a scar remains—not damage, but the memory of becoming animated.

features.name: learned-gesture
features.desc-on-touch: You watch the shore make a gesture it learned over years. The water answers with its own practice.

features.name: repair-tide
features.desc-on-touch: Nothing is broken anymore, but the archive here reads all damage as a form of learning. The tide returns what was taken.

features.name: teaching-undertow
features.desc-on-touch: Beneath the surface, the water teaches the shore what only flowing things can know. The undertow is a lesson written deep.

inscription: the shore learned to swim by becoming the water's practice; repair happened here and the coast keeps moving

reverie.title: REVERIE — the shore where you learned to move together
narr: The water was cold. You waded side by side.
She said the coast was learning. You believed her.
Waves taught you both the same rhythm, the same reach.
The scar in the sand was not damage, she said.
It was where the ground learned to follow water home.

exits.label: back to where the spiral learned to close
into deeper water where shores forget to return
along the taught strand to where repair continues
to the dunes where the learning accumulates
